title: Chapter 192: You're as Good as a Real Ghost
html:
Chen Ge had discovered the “ghost” beneath the crib, though the “ghost” remained unaware.

“Come on out, brother.” Chen Ge pushed the crib aside, pulling the wire attached to the mannequin taut. A slender man lay beneath it, clutching a remote control. Grotesque makeup covered his face, and fake blood drenched his clothes.

“What am I supposed to find in here?” Feeling that the question might be too direct, Chen Ge added, “The security guard gave me no instructions, so perhaps you can help.”

The “ghost” said nothing. He scrambled up and fled the room, catching Chen Ge by surprise.

“Why did he run?” To keep his heart rate steady, Chen Ge did not pursue him. Instead, he continued at the leisurely pace he had maintained since entering. “A baby tugging at your clothes is too simple. There must be a larger scare. The actor probably jumps out when the visitor leaves.”

Picking up the infant mannequin, Chen Ge concluded that its makeup still fell short of his own work.

Xu Zhenzhen?The blanket underneath the baby had this name on it. Why is it her again?

He checked every nearby mannequin and found the same name beneath each one.

I’ve seen this name everywhere since entering. Is it some kind of psychological trick?A search of the nursery eventually uncovered a clue in one crib: a key-shaped pendant resting on a note that read, “For my daughter, Xu Zhenzhen.”

Taking something that belonged to the victim will give someone the impression that they’re haunted by the dead victim. This note is probably supposed to increase the visitors’ fear toward Xu Zhenzhen.

The pendant was necessary to continue; refusing to take it would halt his progress. This was another of the Haunted House’s tricks.

After pocketing it, Chen Ge studied the note. He drew out the Pen Spirit’s ballpoint pen and, imitating the handwriting, added two words to the back: “I’ve written.”

A little surprise for them.

Having exposed the room’s scare, Chen Ge headed for the exit. As he stepped out, wheels rattled in the darkness. A woman with tangled hair, a blood-covered face, and a swollen belly hurtled toward him with a cart full of babies. Most horrifying of all, she had no legs.

Chen Ge’s heart rate rose slightly, then settled. The woman clung close to the left wall—the same wall he had identified as suspicious before entering the nursery.

She was not actually pushing the cart but sitting inside it while a mechanism propelled it. In the narrow corridor, the vehicle moved so quickly that the “pregnant ghost” seemed to flash past him.

Her resentful glare locked onto Chen Ge from barely eight inches away.

So, the scariest thing is outside the room; that’s quite an ingenious design.

Visitors would grow anxious while searching the nursery, then relax in relief once they found the key. That made them completely unprepared for the ghost waiting outside.

There are no tracks on the floor, so is there a machine inside the wall that pushes the cart?

As the cart retracted, Chen Ge followed on silent feet. Unaware that he was behind her, the “pregnant ghost” reveled in the thrill of frightening visitors and turned, hoping to scare him a second time.

Instead, she found his intensely curious face inches away. Surprise froze her expression.

“So, you’ve been squatting inside the cart; that’s quite creative.”

The motorized cart made the woman its driver. For visitor safety, half its base connected to machinery inside the wall, limiting its travel to a single meter.

“This design is excellent, and your expression genuinely affected me. Resentment mixed with hatred—you looked almost like a real ghost.” Chen Ge was generous with sincere praise. The “pregnant ghost” had no idea how to respond. In years of performing, no visitor had ever complimented her acting inside the attraction.

Guests rarely noticed such details. The actors were dancers in the dark, devoted to their craft but seldom appreciated; some visitors even lashed out at them. Though reluctant to admit it, she enjoyed the praise.

“It’s nothing…” Perhaps she had been a ghost for too long, but even her voice sounded grim.

“I’m not kidding. Your gaze was similar to an actual ghost. You are an excellent actor.”

Key in hand, Chen Ge continued to the next scene. Only after he left did the woman realize something. “What did he mean by ‘like a real ghost’? It sounded as though he’s seen one before.”

Beyond the nursery lay a bathroom where several mannequins hung upside down. Tian Teng Medical School relied primarily on visual shocks like these. Their immediate impact kept ordinary visitors screaming.

Chen Ge’s Haunted House followed a different philosophy. Its atmosphere slowly gathered the fear in a visitor’s heart, then released it all at once in a scare that reverberated through the soul.

The bathroom, examination room, and doctors’ lounge contained no actors, relying instead on mechanical effects. In other words, they served as recovery rooms between major scares. Conventional tricks and gore had no effect on Chen Ge. He passed all three easily and found a differently colored key pendant hidden in each. Together with those from the heart and nursery, he now carried five keys.

All of the keys have different colors, so there should only be one real key.

Chen Ge pocketed all the keys and entered the fourth room. The room was small and had the décor from decades ago.

Yellowed paint covered the walls, and a chandelier swayed in the draft. A “corpse” lay across the desk, while a plastic knife and several bloodstained patient files littered the floor.

Bloody handprints marked the ceiling, and chaotic footprints covered the floor. The office looked as though a horde of ghosts had ransacked it.

This is interesting. Why is the dead body’s frame so similar to the young man that was hiding under the crib earlier?

Chen Ge walked to the office table and found something interesting. On the bookshelf behind the table sat an old-fashioned tape recorder that was no longer in production.
